reasoning.step1:
I will identify invoice indicators, locate required fields, consider alternatives, and decide whether any values must be left empty per the No Inference rule.

1) Classification check
- Document contains prominent headings “Rechnung” and repeated “Nummer” / “Datum” and invoice-like sections (positions, sums, VAT). No exclusion terms like “Mahnung” or “Zahlungserinnerung” dominating. Conclusion: this is an invoice — proceed to extraction.

2) Locate Invoice.Date
- I see "Datum 29.01.2024" near the top. That is the invoice issue date. Alternative possibilities: other dates present (Lieferschein date 29.01.2024, Auftragsnr. date 22.01.2024). The clearly labeled "Datum" next to "Nummer" is the invoice date. Extract: "29.01.2024".

3) Locate GrandTotal.Amount
- The document shows "Gesamtbetrag Brutto 493,13 EUR" and also later "Zahlbetrag 473,98 EUR" after skonto. The schema requests "Total payable amount on the invoice". Interpreting "Total payable amount" — potential candidates: gross total before discount (493,13), payable after discounts/skonto (Zahlbetrag 473,98). The label "Zahlbetrag" explicitly means amount to pay. Choose Zahlbetrag 473,98 as GrandTotal.Amount. Keep decimals as in text. No currency symbol per schema? Schema type is number; will strip currency when producing final JSON.

4) Locate Sender.VatId
- Two VAT IDs appear: "Ihre Ust-Id-Nr. ATU64131246" (customer?) and header shows "Ust.-ID-Nr. ATU69710958" in footer (company registration info). Need sender (invoice issuer) VAT. Header lists company CREATON GmbH and lower footer lists "Ust.-ID-Nr. ATU69710958" associated with CREATON. The "Ihre Ust-Id-Nr. ATU64131246" is labeled "Ihre" (your VAT ID = recipient). The sender VAT is ATU69710958. Extract as string "ATU69710958".

5) Locate VAT groups (Vat.Rate, Net.Amount, Vat.Amount)
- The invoice shows tax grouping: "R2 - 20,00% USt auf 410,94 ... 82,19 EUR". That indicates a VAT rate 20.00%, net base 410,94 and VAT amount 82,19. Confirm net totals earlier: "Gesamtbetrag Netto 410,94 EUR" matches. Alternatives: There is also mention of skonto and amounts after discount, but VAT grouping clearly refers to 410,94 net and VAT 82,19. Extract Vat.Rate as 20.00 (rule: remove % symbol; schema number should preserve decimals as in input — input shows "20.00%" or "20,00%"? Text shows "20.00%" in one line and "20,00%" elsewhere. The exact line "20.00%" appears next to R2 in layout: "R2           20.00%                                               82,19 EUR". Also earlier "R2 - 20,00% USt auf 410,94". Need to preserve decimals: choose 20.00 or 20? Rule: extract rates without percent sign, keep decimals same as input. I'll record 20.00.

- Net.Amount: net 410,94 (use comma decimal in source). Schema requires number with same decimal places; convert to dot decimal for JSON number. Preserve two decimals: 410.94.

- Vat.Amount: 82,19 -> 82.19.

6) Verify No Inference and Missing Fields
- All required schema fields located: GrandTotal.Amount (473.98), Invoice.Date (29.01.2024), Sender.VatId (ATU69710958), Vat.Rate (20.00), Net.Amount (410.94), Vat.Amount (82.19). No need to guess other values.

7) Multiple occurrences
- VAT group appears once (R2). No additional Vat.Item entries needed.

End of reasoning.
